html:
The Imamate of Futa Toro was an Islamic state of the Fula-speaking Toucouleur people in the middle Senegal River valley, in what is now northern Senegal and southern Mauritania. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900.

The valley was the land of the medieval Takrur. In 1776 Muslim scholars, the Torodbe, overthrew the Denianke kings and set up an imamate ruled by an elected almamy, following the example of Futa Jallon.

Futa Toro was the homeland of Umar Tall, who in the 1850s drew thousands of its people east to fight in the jihad that built the Tukular Caliphate. Meanwhile the French of Senegal pushed up the river. Governor Faidherbe annexed parts of the valley from 1859, and the last independent leader, Abdul Bokar Kane, was killed in 1891.
